entry.title: Block-wide Signature Aggregation via SNARKs
entry.summary:
Understanding the specific CPU/GPU requirements for various provers is crucial in assessing their impact on network participants. There is a growing concern about introducing roles within networks that demand significant hardware capabilities, as this might deter participation due to high costs. An example cited from a presentation by [@jamesob at OPNext 2025](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=27Qs31E80cA) suggests that it is possible to model these compute requirements explicitly. This approach would provide clear, quantitative insights into what each network participant would need in terms of hardware.
The current centralized nature of mining exacerbates the issue of hardware constraints. Adding more hardware-intensive roles could potentially skew the balance of power within the network's consensus mechanisms. This is particularly sensitive in environments where the equilibrium of game theory plays a critical role in maintaining fair and decentralized control. The suggestion to quantify hardware needs aligns with the need for meticulous planning and research, aimed at sustaining an equitable distribution of power and responsibility among miners and other stakeholders. This proactive inquiry is intended to guide future research directions, ensuring that any new implementations are both practical and considerate of the existing dynamics within the network.
